hints: Use the sector area formula $\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} r^2 \theta$ with $r = 8$ cm and $\text{Area} = \frac{16\pi}{3}\text{ cm}^2$ to find the central angle $\theta$ in radians.
Calculate the arc length $BC$ using $s = r\theta$.
Calculate the length of chord $BC$ using the cosine rule $BC^2 = r^2 + r^2 - 2r^2\cos\theta$ (or $BC = 2r\sin(\theta/2)$).
Add the arc length and chord length to obtain the perimeter of segment $BCD$.
walkthrough:
Set up the sector area equation to find the central angle $\theta$:
$$\frac{1}{2} r^2 \theta = \frac{16\pi}{3} \implies \frac{1}{2}(8^2)\theta = \frac{16\pi}{3} \implies 32\theta = \frac{16\pi}{3} \implies \theta = \frac{\pi}{6}\text{ rad}$$

Calculate the arc length $BC$:
$$\text{Arc } BC = r\theta = 8 \times \frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{4\pi}{3} \approx 4.18879\text{ cm}$$

Calculate the chord length $BC$ using the isosceles triangle formula or cosine rule:
$$BC = 2r\sin\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right) = 2(8)\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{12}\right) = 16\sin(15^\circ) \approx 4.14110\text{ cm}$$

Sum the arc length and chord length to find the total perimeter of the segment:
$$\text{Perimeter} = \text{Arc } BC + \text{Chord } BC = 4.18879 + 4.14110 \approx 8.33\text{ cm}$$

ai_rubric.Circular Measure - Angle in Radians: Finds central angle $\theta = \frac{\pi}{6}$ rad from sector area $\frac{1}{2}(8^2)\theta = \frac{16\pi}{3}$.
ai_rubric.Calculating Perimeters: Calculates arc length $\frac{4\pi}{3} \approx 4.189$ cm and chord length $16\sin(\pi/12) \approx 4.141$ cm, summing to get perimeter $8.33$ cm.
